## D'Andre Swift

Swift is healthy. I found no 2026 injury report on him, and my searches mostly returned 2025 items, so I couldn't verify practice reports beyond the Stat Hub status of Healthy. He has 17.3 pts/g over 8 games (20.0 over the last 4), and his usage is rising. Opportunity share is 35% over the last 4 against 32% for the season, snaps are 70%, and he has 18.5 carries/g and 4.3 targets/g. The touchdown work is the reason he scores. He has 10 rush TDs, 19 goal-line carries (11 in the last 4) and 36 red zone carries. The efficiency is poor. He averages 3.8 yds/carry (3.2 over the last 4) and 5.6 yds/target, and his Monday night line was 27 carries for 69 yards and three TDs, with a longest run of 7 yards. That makes it touchdown-driven production that could fade.

The teammate factor is Kyle Monangai. He has been out since Week 4 with turf toe (about a month), and coach Ben Johnson called it a "bigger deal" than first thought. The Stat Hub lists him as Questionable and set to return. Turf toe tends to linger. It limits cutting and push-off, and re-aggravation is common, so a first game back usually means a reduced role. I couldn't confirm his final Week 9 status. His 23% season share is mostly early-season work, so the model applies a ×0.9 cut. Roschon Johnson sits at 14% opportunity share over the last 4.

The Week 9 matchup is against TB, which the Stat Hub calls the toughest RB matchup (14.5 pts/g allowed to RBs, ×0.86). Projection is 14.8, with a floor of 7.8 and a ceiling of 19.1. Rest-of-season projection is 136.4.

## Bucky Irving

Irving is healthy per the Stat Hub. My searches returned only 2025 foot and shoulder injury stories, which I'm ignoring, so I couldn't verify anything current. He has 15.2 pts/g for the season but 20.2 over the last 4, and his workload has grown. Opportunity share is 40% over the last 4 against 36% for the season, carries are 22.8/g, and he put up 27 carries for 170 yards against Atlanta. He averages 5.0 yds/carry (5.4 over the last 4). The weak spots are receiving and goal-line work. He has 2.0 targets/g, 4.3 rec yds/g and 2.1 yds/target over the last 4, and only 5 goal-line carries all season. His 22 red zone carries over the last 4 are real, but he often doesn't finish them. Snaps are 62%. Kenny Gainwell takes 20% of the opportunities, and nothing in what I found suggests that role is changing.

Week 9 is at CHI, the 3rd toughest RB matchup (15.9 pts/g allowed, ×0.90). Projection is 16.4, with a floor of 5.7 and a ceiling of 20.5. Rest-of-season projection is 141.0. Tampa's offense had no completed passes last week, and that run-heavy script is unlikely to repeat. His floor depends on the Bucs staying on the ground.

## The verdict

**Rest of season: Irving, narrowly (141.0 vs 136.4).** His volume is higher, his efficiency is much better, and his workload keeps climbing. Swift's value depends on touchdowns, and a returning Monangai threatens that share.

**This week: Irving (16.4 vs 14.8).** Swift has the worse matchup (the toughest RB matchup) and a possible Monangai return, and the model drops his projection about 14% for those two factors. Irving's matchup is also hard, but his carry volume is more dependable. Start both if you have to. If you're choosing one, start Irving, and don't sell Swift for less than a clear upgrade.
